content.why_title: Why Use a Visual CSS Grid Generator?
content.why_desc: CSS Grid is the most powerful layout system in CSS, but its syntax — grid-template-columns, grid-template-rows, fr units, minmax(), repeat() — has a steep learning curve. Our visual generator lets you configure your grid via sliders and dropdowns and watch your layout update instantly, so you understand what each property does without digging through MDN documentation.

fr.title: ✓ Prefer fr Units Over Percentages
fr.desc: The fr (fraction) unit distributes available space after fixed-size columns, avoiding the need to manually calculate percentages for flexible columns.

minmax.title: ✓ Use minmax() for Responsive Grids
minmax.desc: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(250px, 1fr)) creates a responsive grid that automatically adjusts the number of columns to fit the container — no media queries needed.

named.title: ✓ Use Named Grid Areas for Page Layouts
named.desc: grid-template-areas with named cells (header, sidebar, main, footer) makes page-level layouts readable and easy to modify.

auto.title: ✓ Understand auto-fill vs auto-fit
auto.desc: auto-fill creates as many tracks as will fit (leaving empty ones). auto-fit collapses empty tracks and stretches existing items to fill — usually more useful for card grids.

faq.q1: What is a fr unit in CSS Grid?
faq.a1: fr stands for 'fractional unit'. 1fr represents one fraction of the available free space in the grid container. repeat(3, 1fr) creates 3 equal columns that share all available space equally.
faq.q2: How is CSS Grid different from Flexbox?
faq.a2: Flexbox is one-dimensional — it arranges items along a single axis (row or column). CSS Grid is two-dimensional — it controls both rows and columns simultaneously, making it far more powerful for page-level layouts.
faq.a3: minmax(min, max) defines a size range for a grid track. minmax(200px, 1fr) means a column is at least 200px wide but grows up to take available space — perfect for responsive grids.
faq.q4: When should I use CSS Grid vs Flexbox?
faq.a4: Use Grid for 2D page layouts where you need both row and column control simultaneously. Use Flexbox for 1D component layouts like navbars, button groups, and form rows. Most modern layouts use both — Grid for the overall structure, Flexbox for component internals.
